:::{#def-supremum}
#### Supremum (least upper bound)

Let $A \subseteq \reals$ be nonempty
and bounded above,
meaning that some $t \in \reals$ satisfies $a \le t$ for all $a \in A$.
The **supremum** of $A$,
written $\sup A$,
is the smallest real number $t$ satisfying $a \le t$ for all $a \in A$:

$$\sup A \eqdef \min\cb{t \in \reals : \all a \in A,\ a \le t}$$

If $A$ is nonempty but not bounded above,
we write $\sup A = +\infty$ by convention.

:::

::: notes
The minimum in @def-supremum always exists:
that is the completeness (least-upper-bound) property of the real numbers
[@rudin1976principles, Definition 1.8, p. 4, and Theorem 1.19, p. 8].
If the supremum belongs to $A$, it equals the maximum: $\sup A = \max A$.
:::
